title: Cocktail 2 Just Got an 'A.' The Diaspora's Tickets Are Already Live in New York, London and Toronto.
excerpt: Homi Adajania's sequel lands an adult certificate, a chart-topping trailer in eight countries, and same-day overseas booking — fourteen years after Deepika made Cocktail a generation's heartbreak.
body:
It took a profanity swap, a "Jew on the run" line on the cutting room floor, and one little letter — **A** — to make **Cocktail 2** the most grown-up cocktail Bollywood has served all summer. And the diaspora is already in the queue.

Fourteen years after **Deepika Padukone**, **Saif Ali Khan** and **Diana Penty** turned a Spanish summer into a generation's heartbreak, the spiritual sequel pours into cinemas worldwide this Friday, June 19. Only this time the bartenders are new — **Shahid Kapoor**, **Kriti Sanon** and **Rashmika Mandanna** — and director **Homi Adajania** has mixed it stronger. The Central Board of Film Certification has handed the film an adult certificate, clearing it with no visual cuts and only a couple of audio nips. It's a quietly seismic moment for the cast: Kriti Sanon, the girl-next-door of a hundred breezy rom-coms, has never carried an A-rated film before. For Rashmika, it's only her second after the bruising spectacle of *Animal*. For Shahid, an A is practically a love language — this is his fifth, sitting alongside *Kabir Singh*, *Udta Punjab*, *Kaminey* and this year's *O'Romeo*.

> "From friends to lovers to chaos, the perfect cocktail is back." — the film's own tagline

What the certificate really signals is intent. The original *Cocktail* flirted; this one, by all accounts, doesn't bother with the buttons. The trailer leans into a slicker, more adult register — Sicilian coastlines, a "seductive dance sequence" tucked into the foot-tapping *Mashooqa*, and an Arijit Singh ballad, *Tujhko*, that frames Shahid and Rashmika as college sweethearts torn apart by circumstance. Anaita Shroff Adajania's costumes glitter, Santhana Krishnan Ravichandran's camera drinks in the Mediterranean light, and Pritam's soundtrack does the thing Pritam soundtracks do — it gets into your bloodstream before you've decided whether you like the film.

The numbers say the world has already decided it's curious. That trailer climbed to **No. 1 on YouTube's Movie Trailer Charts across eight countries** — India, the UK, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain and Kuwait — and cracked the Top 10 in the United States. In India, advance bookings crossed **₹3 crore** with reserved seats, with over 47,000 tickets sold by Wednesday evening and Delhi emerging as the strongest day-one market. It's not blockbuster-opener territory yet, but for a romantic entertainer driven by urban multiplex crowds, the trajectory is healthy — and the real spike traditionally comes Thursday night and Friday morning, once word of mouth kicks in.

### Where the diaspora comes in

Here's the part that matters if you're reading this from a kitchen in Edison or a flat in Wembley: **Cocktail 2's overseas advance bookings are now open.** Distributor Marudhar Entertainment has confirmed the film releases internationally on June 19, the same day as India — no agonising weeks-long wait, no hunting for a grainy stream. Tickets are live across the **United States, United Kingdom, Canada, the Gulf, Australia, New Zealand and key European markets.**

That simultaneity is the quiet flex of post-pandemic Hindi cinema. A film like this used to trickle out to NRI audiences as an afterthought. Now North America and the UK are treated as front-line territories, courted with their own booking windows and trailer-chart bragging rights. The fact that *Cocktail 2* topped the Gulf charts so emphatically tells you exactly who the marketing team is dressing up for — and the answer is the same desi crowd that turned the first film's *Tum Hi Ho Bandhu* and *Daaru Desi* into wedding-sangeet staples a decade ago.

### Can it bottle the magic?

The pressure, of course, is the ghost of 2012. The original *Cocktail* gave us Veronica — Deepika's wild, wounded, unforgettable party girl — and a love triangle that people still argue about at brunch. Adajania returns to that emotional architecture but swaps the cast wholesale, betting that Shahid's brooding charisma and the never-before-seen pairing with Rashmika (their "fresh chemistry," as the trade keeps calling it) can strike the same nerve. Kriti, marking her second film with Shahid after *Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya*, gets to play against type in a role early reactions are describing as her most unbuttoned yet.

At two hours and thirty minutes, with an A-certificate and a Pritam album already in heavy rotation, *Cocktail 2* isn't trying to be the comfort-watch original. It's trying to be the louder, sexier, more dangerous one. Whether that's a glow-up or a gamble, the diaspora gets to find out at the same moment Mumbai does — Friday, in a theatre near you. Pour responsibly.
